title: FDR Fireside Chats
paragraphs: Roosevelt radio addresses corresponding to the FDR Presidential Library list of 31 speeches identified as Fireside Chats. Institutional audiovisual guidance explicitly says the category is disputed: 28 definite, two questionable, and potentially as many as 33 under an extended definition.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Depression and New Deal chats (March 12, 1933 to June 24, 1938), European war, defense and U.S. entry (September 3, 1939 to December 9, 1941), and World War II home-front and war-progress chats (February 23, 1942 to January 6, 1945).
Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Franklin D. Roosevelt (speaker).

The stories often return to World War II, military progress and diplomacy, wartime home front, labor, prices and mobilization, New Deal recovery and federal programs, employment, relief, WPA and social security, economic conditions, prices and sacrifice, and national defense, emergency and military readiness.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Presidential radio communication and the Fireside Chat form, Great Depression and New Deal public explanation, European war and American defense mobilization, and World War II home front and military progress.
